{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01St5tUdjXuZeS5XTajXXCu3","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Office Ally, LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://cms.officeally.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Office Ally, LLC is a healthcare technology company founded in 2000, headquartered in Brentwood, TN with additional offices in Salt Lake City, UT, San Antonio, TX, and Vancouver, WA (technology headquarters). The company serves more than 80,000 healthcare organizations of all sizes, from startups to Fortune 100 companies. It has approximately 300+ employees.\n     9→\n    10→Office Ally's core business began with claims clearinghouse services and has expanded into a full suite of cloud-based healthcare administrative and clinical tools. The company positions itself primarily around revenue cycle management and administrative workflow, with the EHR being one product in a broader ecosystem. The company processes over 250 billion dollars in claims value annually and connects to 6,100+ payers, supporting 1.4M+ NPIs. Office Ally competes with NextGen Healthcare, AdvancedMD, and similar mid-market ambulatory healthcare IT vendors.\n    11→\n    12→The company's product suite includes five core offerings: Service Center (clearinghouse/claims portal), Practice Mate (free practice management), EHR 24/7 (clinical EHR), EDI Clearinghouse (enterprise API), and Insurance Discovery (revenue recovery). The suite is designed to work together as an integrated platform, though each component can also be used independently. The pricing model is notable in the industry: Practice Mate (PM) is free with transactional fees, and EHR 24/7 is $44.95/month per provider — one of the lowest-cost EHRs on the market. This low-cost, bundled approach targets small to mid-size ambulatory practices that need affordable, no-frills solutions.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: EHR 24/7\n    15→\n    16→CHPL IDs: 11572\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→EHR 24/7 is a web-based, cloud-hosted electronic health record system designed for ambulatory medical practices across all specialties. It is certified under the ONC 2015 Edition Cures Update (certification date: 2024-12-26, version 5.9.255). The product has broad certification coverage including clinical documentation (a)(1)-(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3), patient portal (e)(1), public health reporting (f)(1), (f)(5), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10).\n    21→\n    22→EHR 24/7 is part of a larger Office Ally ecosystem but is the certified Health IT Module. It is designed to work in tandem with Practice Mate (the free PM system) and integrates with the Service Center clearinghouse, Patient Ally portal, and various add-on services. The EHR is not a standalone silo — it shares patient data, scheduling, and billing workflows with Practice Mate and the clearinghouse.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→The intended users are \"Physicians, Nurses, and Office Staff\" per the CHPL certification. EHR 24/7 is used by more than 20,000 users (per EMRFinder) within Office Ally's broader 80,000+ organization customer base. The product targets:\n    27→\n    28→- Small to mid-size ambulatory practices\n    29→- Solo practitioners and small group practices\n    30→- Multi-specialty practices (the vendor markets it as suitable for \"all medical specialties and sizes\")\n    31→- Budget-conscious practices that need affordable EHR/PM solutions\n    32→\n    33→User reviews on Capterra (4.6/5 rating), EMRFinder (4/5), and other sites indicate the product is particularly popular with small practices seeking low-cost, functional EHR solutions. Reviewers frequently mention using it alongside Practice Mate for billing and the Service Center for claims submission. Common user roles include physicians, office managers, billing staff, and clinical social workers.\n    34→\n    35→### Modules & Functionality\n    36→\n    37→Based on vendor materials, product pages, support documentation, and third-party reviews, EHR 24/7 includes the following functionality:\n    38→\n    39→**Clinical Charting & Documentation:**\n    40→- Customizable SOAP notes with templates and user-defined phrases\n    41→- Progress note workflows (including short-form nurse notes)\n    42→- Medical history documentation\n    43→- Diagnosis and treatment recording\n    44→- Customizable clinical templates with drag-and-drop functionality\n    45→- Clinical summaries generated from individual progress notes\n    46→- Document management (storage of images, test results, clinical notes)\n    47→\n    48→**Patient Demographics & Records:**\n    49→- Patient record creation and management\n    50→- Merging duplicate patient records\n    51→- Transferring patient encounters between charts\n    52→- Confidential information storage with access controls\n    53→- Patient intake forms (Intake Pro add-on for digital check-in)\n    54→\n    55→**Medications & Prescribing:**\n    56→- Medication list management within progress notes and separately\n    57→- E-prescribing via OA-Rx add-on (electronic transmission to pharmacies)\n    58→- EPCS (Electronic Superbills and charge capture\n   165→- Patient billing records (invoices, copays, balances, payments)\n   166→- Patient ledger entries\n   167→\n   168→**Communication and portal data:**\n   169→- The company serves more than 80,000 healthcare organizations of all sizes, from startups to Fortune 100 companies. It has approximately 300+ employees.\n\nOffice Ally's core business began with claims clearinghouse services and has expanded into a full suite of cloud-based healthcare administrative and clinical tools. The company positions itself primarily around revenue cycle management and administrative workflow, with the EHR being one product in a broader ecosystem. The company processes over 250 billion dollars in claims value annually and connects to 6,100+ payers, supporting 1.4M+ NPIs. Office Ally competes with NextGen Healthcare, AdvancedMD, and similar mid-market ambulatory healthcare IT vendors.\n\nThe company's product suite includes five core offerings: Service Center (clearinghouse/claims portal), Practice Mate (free practice management), EHR 24/7 (clinical EHR), EDI Clearinghouse (enterprise API), and Insurance Discovery (revenue recovery). The suite is designed to work together as an integrated platform, though each component can also be used independently. The pricing model is notable in the industry: Practice Mate (PM) is free with transactional fees, and EHR 24/7 is $44.95/month per provider — one of the lowest-cost EHRs on the market. This low-cost, bundled approach targets small to mid-size ambulatory practices that need affordable, no-frills solutions.\n\n## Product: EHR 24/7\n\nCHPL IDs: 11572\n\n### What It Is\n\nEHR 24/7 is a web-based, cloud-hosted electronic health record system designed for ambulatory medical practices across all specialties. It is certified under the ONC 2015 Edition Cures Update (certification date: 2024-12-26, version 5.9.255). The product has broad certification coverage including clinical documentation (a)(1)-(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3), patient portal (e)(1), public health reporting (f)(1), (f)(5), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10).\n\nEHR 24/7 is part of a larger Office Ally ecosystem but is the certified Health IT Module. It is designed to work in tandem with Practice Mate (the free PM system) and integrates with the Service Center clearinghouse, Patient Ally portal, and various add-on services. The EHR is not a standalone silo — it shares patient data, scheduling, and billing workflows with Practice Mate and the clearinghouse.\n\n### Users & Market\n\nThe intended users are \"Physicians, Nurses, and Office Staff\" per the CHPL certification. EHR 24/7 is used by more than 20,000 users (per EMRFinder) within Office Ally's broader 80,000+ organization customer base. The product targets:\n\n- Small to mid-size ambulatory practices\n- Solo practitioners and small group practices\n- Multi-specialty practices (the vendor markets it as suitable for \"all medical specialties and sizes\")\n- Budget-conscious practices that need affordable EHR/PM solutions\n\nUser reviews on Capterra (4.6/5 rating), EMRFinder (4/5), and other sites indicate the product is particularly popular with small practices seeking low-cost, functional EHR solutions. Reviewers frequently mention using it alongside Practice Mate for billing and the Service Center for claims submission. Common user roles include physicians, office managers, billing staff, and clinical social workers.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor materials, product pages, support documentation, and third-party reviews, EHR 24/7 includes the following functionality:\n\n**Clinical Charting & Documentation:**\n- Customizable SOAP notes with templates and user-defined phrases\n- Progress note workflows (including short-form nurse notes)\n- Medical history documentation\n- Diagnosis and treatment recording\n- Customizable clinical templates with drag-and-drop functionality\n- Clinical summaries generated from individual progress notes\n- Document management (storage of images, test results, clinical notes)\n\n**Patient Demographics & Records:**\n- Patient record creation and management\n- Merging duplicate patient records\n- Transferring patient encounters between charts\n- Confidential information storage with access controls\n- Patient intake forms (Intake Pro add-on for digital check-in)\n\n**Medications & Prescribing:**\n- Medication list management within progress notes and separately\n- E-prescribing via OA-Rx add-on (electronic transmission to pharmacies)\n- EPCS (Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances) available as add-on ($100/yr per provider)\n- Medication refill requests (via Patient Ally portal)\n- Fullscript supplement prescribing integration\n\n**Allergies & Problem Lists:**\n- Allergy recording and management\n- Problem list management (implied by (a)(5) certification for demographics)\n\n**Vitals & Clinical Data:**\n- Vital signs recording\n- Blood sugar logs\n- Medical history tracking\n\n**Immunizations:**\n- Immunization recording in patient charts\n- Immunization registry submission (certified for (f)(1) immunization registry reporting)\n\n**Lab & Radiology:**\n- Lab order creation and management within the system\n- Radiology order tracking\n- Integration with external laboratory information systems (LIS) for order transmission and result receipt\n- Lab/HIE interfacing\n- Referral order tracking\n\n**Scheduling & Appointments:**\n- Appointment scheduling (integrated with Practice Mate)\n- SMS check-in\n- Automated appointment reminders (Reminder Mate add-on — text, call, email)\n- Patient self-service appointment scheduling (via Patient Ally portal)\n\n**Billing & Claims (via Practice Mate integration):**\n- Patient billing and invoicing (copays, balances)\n- Configurable superbills with custom code capture\n- Patient ledger\n- Insurance eligibility and benefits verification (270/271 transactions)\n- Claims submission to 5,000+ payers via Service Center\n- Claims status tracking\n- Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA)\n- Statement mailing (add-on for automated patient billing statements)\n\n**Patient Portal (Patient Ally):**\n- Free patient portal providing 24/7 access to health information\n- View medical records, lab results, visit notes, medications, immunization records\n- Request appointments\n- Send/receive secure messages with providers\n- Request medication refills\n- Complete patient intake forms digitally\n- Make and track payments\n- View medical history, diagnosis, and medications\n\n**Telehealth:**\n- HIPAA-compliant virtual visits as add-on\n- Secure online video consultations\n\n**Secure Messaging & Communication:**\n- Updox Messaging (HIPAA-compliant patient messaging add-on, $6/user/month)\n- Secure Direct messaging for provider-to-provider communication\n- Patient messaging through portal\n\n**Reporting & Analytics:**\n- Audit log reporting\n- PHI disclosure documentation\n- E-prescription reporting\n- Reports module in Practice Mate\n- (Reviews note reporting features are relatively weak/basic)\n\n**Public Health Reporting:**\n- Immunization registry reporting (f)(1)\n- Cancer registry reporting (f)(5)\n\n**Interoperability:**\n- FHIR API access (g)(7)-(g)(10) — certified for patient and population service APIs\n- Clinical information exchange / transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3) — C-CDA generation and receipt\n- Health Information Exchange (HIE) interfacing\n- CCDA clinical summaries\n\n**Clinical Decision Support:**\n- Certified for (a)(12) family health history and (a)(14) implantable device list\n- CDS interventions (implied by (a)(1) CPOE and related certifications)\n- Drug interaction checking (implied by e-prescribing)\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features and modules described above, EHR 24/7 (along with its integrated ecosystem) stores and manages the following types of data:\n\n**Clinical data directly evidenced by vendor materials and support docs:**\n- Patient demographics and contact information\n- Medical history (past medical, family, social)\n- Progress notes / encounter documentation (SOAP notes)\n- Vital signs and blood sugar logs\n- Allergies\n- Medication lists and prescription history\n- Immunization records\n- Lab orders and results (via LIS integration)\n- Radiology orders\n- Referral orders\n- Diagnoses and problem lists\n- Clinical summaries (C-CDA documents)\n- Clinical documents and images\n- Family health history (certified (a)(12))\n- Implantable device list (certified (a)(14))\n\n**Administrative and billing data (via Practice Mate/Service Center integration):**\n- Appointment schedules\n- Insurance eligibility and benefits information\n- Claims data (submissions, statuses, remittances)\n- Superbills and charge capture\n- Patient billing records (invoices, copays, balances, payments)\n- Patient ledger entries\n\n**Communication and portal data:**\n- Patient-provider messages (via Patient Ally and Updox)\n- Provider-to-provider secure Direct messages\n- Patient intake form submissions\n- Appointment requests\n\n**Audit and compliance data:**\n- Audit logs\n- PHI disclosure records\n- E-prescription reports\n\n**Gaps and uncertainties:**\n- The vendor website does not mention growth charts or pediatric-specific features, so it's unclear whether these are supported despite the \"all specialties\" marketing.\n- Clinical decision support specifics are not well-documented beyond what's implied by ONC certification criteria.\n- Reporting capabilities are described by reviewers as relatively basic/weak — it's unclear how much structured analytics data the system stores vs. displays.\n- The {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015vvWVFwPbVhcyn2Si7qYi7","type":"tool_result","content":"170.315 (b)(10) EHI Export Documentation\nOffice Ally provides an export of electronic health information (EHI) for a single patient as well\nas for a patient population in the following computable formats:\n1. CCDA:\nOffice Ally EHR 24/7 supports bulk export of HL7 CCDA xml files which comply to\nUnited States Core Data for Interoperability (USCDI), Version 1 requirements.\nThe specifications for the CCDA can be obtained from the HL7 website:\nC-CDA (HL7 CDA® R2 Implementation Guide: Consolidated CDA Templates for\nClinical Notes - US Realm)\n2. Appointments:\n•\n\nThis file offers a comprehensive view of appointment details, the data will be\nexported in CSV format\n\n3. Claims:\n•\n\nThis file offers a comprehensive view of claim details, the data will be exported\nin CSV format\n\n4. Attachments:\n•\n\nContains any scanned or uploaded documents in the patient’s record, the files\nwill be exported in the format in which they were uploaded\n\nProduct Name and Version:\nOffice Ally EHR 24/7 5.6.81\n\nVersion History\nVersion\n1.0.0\n1.0.1\n\nDate\nNovember 30, 2023\nJanuary 18, 2024\n\nComments\nOriginal Draft\nIncluded Attachments and\nupdated Product Version\n\nOffice Ally Electronic Health Information Export Documentation","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cd3b12b2-024c-4dcf-ad96-d3e7b709d3b2","uuid":"1388d19f-d29b-4619-b67c-b0f4c91d641d","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"170.315 (b)(10) EHI Export Documentation\nOffice Ally provides an export of electronic health information (EHI) for a single patient as well\nas for a patient population in the following computable formats:\n1. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RFtjd9LFb9Yh5kayj8yGsJ","type":"tool_result","content":"Costs and Considerations of Certiﬁed Health IT\nCapability\n\nDescription of\nCapability\n\nCost or Fees\n\nContractual\nConsiderations\nConsiderations of a contractual nature\n(including developer policies and other\nbusiness practices) that a user may encounter\nin the implementation or use of the capability\n-OR- in the connection with the data\ngenerated in the course of using the\ncapability.\n\nOfﬁce Ally 24/7TM electronic\nhealth record (EHR)\n[ONC Health IT Certification]\n\nePrescibing (including Drug\nFormularies and Drug to\nDrug/Drug to Allergy\nInteractions)\n\nFully functional EHR program with\nbuilt-in ePrescribing capabilities,\nconnectivity to major Lab Companies\nand Immunization Registries. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_011mRTssUfihPn3C3PkNkrKg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012rdAhUdDgFWwye54x8mfZQ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/office-ally-llc--ehr-24-7/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Office Ally, LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://cms.officeally.com/onc-acb-certification\n- Final URL (after redirect): https://cms.officeally.com/resources/onc-acb-certification\n- CHPL ID: 11572\n- Product: EHR 24/7, version 5.9.255\n- Certification date: 2024-12-26\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — `curl -sI -L \"https://cms.officeally.com/onc-acb-certification\"` returned a 301 redirect to `/resources/onc-acb-certification`, then 200 OK with `Content-Type: text/html`. Served via Cloudflare.\n\n2. **Page fetch** — `curl -sL \"https://cms.officeally.com/onc-acb-certification\" -o /tmp/oa-page.html` returned 123KB of HTML. The page is a Webflow-hosted compliance/certification page titled \"Office Ally's Certified EHR (Electronic Health Records)\".\n\n3. **Page structure** — The page has:\n   - A Drummond Certified seal with buttons for \"Cost and Considerations\", \"Find your CMS Certification ID\", and \"Certificate of Compliance\"\n   - A table showing CMS Certification ID `2025CUD8GVA660Z`, live date 12/26/2024, EHR Version 5.9.255, FHIR 4-B, etc.\n   - \"21st Century CURES Act Certification Real World Test Documents\" section with RWT plans/results for 2022-2025\n   - **\"Electronic Health Information Export\"** section with a single bullet link: \"170.315 (b)(10) EHI Export Documentation\"\n\n4. **Downloaded the EHI Export PDF** —\n   ```\n   curl -sL \"https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6830ce6e8206ddade0c99cae/68b897ca686e527d9b1d1250_20240208%20EHI%20Export%20Documentation.pdf\" -o downloads/EHI_Export_Documentation.pdf\n   ```\n   Confirmed: PDF document, 1 page, 97KB. Author: Mark Vomocil. Created: 2024-02-08 via Microsoft Word.\n\n5. **Checked for additional artifacts** — Searched all links on the page. The only EHI-relevant file is the single PDF. The \"Costs and Considerations\" PDF is a general pricing/feature disclosure document and does not contain EHI export details. No data dictionary, schema files, API documentation, or sample data files were found on the page.\n\n6. **Checked PDF for embedded links/attachments** — `pdfdetach -list` reports 0 embedded files. The PDF text contains links to the HL7 USCDI and C-CDA specifications (external standards, not vendor-specific documentation).\n\n7. **Browser screenshot** — Navigated to the page in Chrome and took a full-page screenshot confirming the page structure described above.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a **single one-page PDF** (dated February 8, 2024, version 1.0.1). It describes four export components:\n\n1. **CCDA** — Bulk export of HL7 C-CDA XML files complying with USCDI Version 1. Links to the HL7 C-CDA specification for format details. No vendor-specific profile documentation, no field mapping, no sample files.\n\n2. **Appointments** — CSV export with \"a comprehensive view of appointment details.\" No field list, no schema, no sample.\n\n3. **Claims** — CSV export with \"a comprehensive view of claim details.\" No field list, no schema, no sample.\n\n4. **Attachments** — Scanned/uploaded documents exported in their original upload format.\n\nThe documentation states the export supports both single-patient and patient-population export. The product version listed in the PDF is 5.6.81 (older than the current certified version 5.9.255).\n\nThere is **no data dictionary** — no table names, no field names, no data types, no value sets, no schema files, no API documentation, no sample data, and no export instructions beyond the four bullet points above.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe export documentation claims four export streams. Here is how they map against the data domains identified in the product research:\n\n**Covered (at least nominally):**\n- Clinical data via C-CDA: demographics, medications, allergies, problems, vital signs, immunizations, lab results, clinical notes, procedures, care plans — to the extent they fit in USCDI v1 / C-CDA\n- Appointments: CSV export mentioned\n- Claims: CSV export mentioned\n- Attachments: scanned/uploaded documents in original format\n\n**Likely missing or ambiguous — not mentioned anywhere in the documentation:**\n- Medication administration records and prescription history beyond what C-CDA captures\n- Referral orders and radiology orders (may partially appear in C-CDA but not guaranteed)\n- Family health history (certified under (a)(12) but not mentioned in export)\n- Implantable device list (certified under (a)(14) but not mentioned in export)\n- Patient billing records: invoices, copays, balances, payments, patient ledger entries — the \"Claims\" CSV likely covers payer claims but not patient-facing billing\n- Insurance/enrollment information\n- Superbills and charge capture detail\n- Patient portal messages and secure messages\n- Patient intake form submissions\n- E-prescribing history and controlled substance prescribing records\n\n**The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) concern:**\nThe C-CDA component is essentially a USCDI v1 clinical summary export — this is the same data that would be available through their (g)(10) FHIR API, just in C-CDA format instead. The Appointments and Claims CSVs represent a genuine attempt to go beyond the USCDI clinical data set, but without field-level documentation it's impossible to assess how comprehensive they are. The export does not describe how it handles data that doesn't fit into C-CDA or the two CSV files — for example, custom clinical templates, SOAP note free text, blood sugar logs, or clinical decision support data.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **C-CDA XML** — a recognized standard, but limited to what USCDI v1 defines. The documentation references USCDI v1 (not v3/v4), which is notably behind the current standard.\n- **CSV** — for appointments and claims. No schema or field definitions provided. Without column headers, data types, or value set documentation, a third party cannot reliably interpret these files.\n- **Native format** — for attachments (scanned documents exported as-is).\n\nThe combination of C-CDA + CSV + attachments is a reasonable multi-format approach, but the complete absence of field-level documentation for the CSV components makes them practically opaque to any recipient.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation possible. The entire documentation is a single page with four bullet points. There are:\n\n- **No field-level definitions** for any export component\n- **No data dictionary** of any kind\n- **No CSV column headers** or schema documentation\n- **No C-CDA template constraints** or customizations beyond referencing the standard\n- **No sample export files** or worked examples\n- **No export instructions** (how does a user trigger the export? Where do they find it in the UI?)\n- **No API documentation** for programmatic access\n- **No relationship documentation** between the export components\n- **No versioning alignment** — the PDF references product version 5.6.81 while the current certified version is 5.9.255\n\nA developer receiving this export would have C-CDA files they could parse with standard tooling, but the CSV files would require reverse-engineering from column headers in the actual export files. The documentation provides no basis for building an import system.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Export type names only. No table names, no field names, no data types.\n- **Coded fields**: Not documented.\n- **Relationships**: Not documented.\n- **Value sets**: Not documented.\n- **Versioning**: The PDF has a two-entry version history (v1.0.0 Nov 2023, v1.0.1 Jan 2024). No updates since then despite the product being re-certified in Dec 2024.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nOffice Ally's EHI export documentation is a compliance checkbox — a single page that acknowledges the existence of an export mechanism without providing the technical detail needed to understand, validate, or use it. The inclusion of Appointments and Claims CSVs alongside C-CDA shows awareness that EHI extends beyond clinical summaries, but the total absence of field-level documentation for these components undermines their utility. The C-CDA component, while referencing a recognized standard, is limited to USCDI v1 and does not address how data outside that scope is handled. Significant data domains stored by EHR 24/7 — patient billing, secure messages, custom templates, specialty-specific clinical data, e-prescribing records — have no documented export path.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://cms.officeally.com/resources/onc-acb-certification\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (curl works fine, browser used for screenshot only)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (one redirect, then a single bullet link to the PDF)\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare present but not blocking)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- None. The page loaded cleanly via curl and browser.
